narrative.overview:
LLM Benchmark Studio is designed as an interactive psychometric monograph and experimental apparatus inspired by Nature Methods and Edward Tufte. Rather than treating multi-model evaluation as a dark-SaaS analytics toy with glowing neon cards, the interface reads like an authoritative scientific publication where every aggregate claim—Cohen's κ, Krippendorff's α, ICC(2,1), and 3-level Verbatim Faithfulness—is transparent, traceable to its mathematical formula, and auditable down to the exact row and corpus quote.

High information density is achieved through typographic hierarchy and horizontal rule discipline rather than decorative chrome. Surfaces sit flat on warm archival paper in light mode (the default) and nocturnal archival slate in dark mode. Double-ruled mastheads, Roman numeral section indices (I., II., III., IV.), tripartite booktabs tables, and tabular monospace matrices keep complex N × N inter-rater comparisons and row-level forensic audits effortlessly scannable during long research sessions.
keyCharacteristics: Archival warm paper ground paired with deep charcoal ink, scholarly JCR crimson accents, and Prussian academic slate telemetry provenance labels.
Tripartite booktabs structural geometry (2px top/bottom ink rules, 1px crisp stone hairlines) replacing heavy box shadows, floating cards, and glassmorphic blur.

Editorial serif headings (Source Serif 4) with Roman numeral indexing (I., II., III., IV., Registro I.) paired with dense functional copy (Source Sans 3) and tabular monospace (JetBrains Mono) for metrics, formulas, and verbatim corpus quotes.
Full methodological transparency ("zero black box") exposing KaTeX equations, variable legends, evaluated field chips, and row-by-row discrepancy inspection.

rules.name: The Crimson Significance Rule
rules.body: Scholarly JCR Crimson is reserved exclusively for the primary interactive decision on a surface, active section state, section ledger prefixes (Registro I.), or the final publication-ready KPI column (such as Pillar IV Convergence or Completed Auditables). Never dilute it across decorative backgrounds or non-actionable badges.

rules.name: The Archival Paper Default Rule
rules.body: Light mode on warm archival cream is the canonical presentation of the workbench; dark mode shifts to nocturnal slate with warm parchment text while preserving identical booktabs rule contrast.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Mandate
rules.body: Every numeric cell, sample size (N = ...), correlation coefficient, percentage, and badge counter must enforce font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so decimals and columns align vertically across rows.

rules.name: The Roman Numeral Indexing Rule
rules.body: Top-level navigation modes, KPI figures, experiment registries (Registro I.), and the four validation pillars are indexed with Roman numerals (I., II., III., IV.) in monospace or serif to reinforce the structure of a multi-part scientific monograph.

rules.name: The Booktabs Over Box-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Major synthesis banners, experiment registries, leaderboards, and KPI figures establish hierarchy with 2px solid top and bottom rules (border-t-2 border-b-2 border-foreground) rather than drop shadows or blurred glass backplates.

dos: Do frame major synthesis headers, KPI strips, experiment registries (Registro I.), and comparative tables with 2px solid charcoal top/bottom rules (border-t-2 border-foreground) and 1px stone hairlines (border-border / divide-border).
Do use Source Serif 4 (font-serif) with Roman numeral prefixes (I., II., III., IV.) for section navigation, pillar headings, registry titles, and top-level KPI figures.

Do apply JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums (font-mono) to all statistical metrics, Prussian Academic Slate provenance sub-labels, sample sizes (N = ...), model IDs, prompt templates, and verbatim quotes.
Do keep surfaces flat (shadow-none) and rectangular (rounded-none on synthesis banners, executive abstracts, and experiment ledgers; rounded-sm / 2px on interactive controls).
Do expose the mathematical formula, evaluated fields, and row-level audit trigger (Eye inspection button) beside every aggregate psychometric metric.
donts: Don't use glassmorphic blur panels (backdrop-blur-xl), glowing drop shadows (shadow-lg shadow-primary/20), or hover scale transforms (hover:scale-[1.02]) on cards or buttons.
Don't use large pill or card border radii (rounded-xl, rounded-2xl) on containers, wizard steppers, buttons, or tables.
Don't introduce off-palette neon accents (such as purple or emerald gradient CTA pills) where Scholarly JCR Crimson (--primary) or Prussian Academic Slate (--accent-foreground) belongs.
Don't render numerical columns or correlation matrices in proportional sans-serif figures without tabular-nums.
